utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seric. Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-PT, the Prosecutor versus Martinovic and Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Seric. I'm sorry, I forget.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, good morning. I apologise for standing up before the case was called. However, I have a request to make. I don't really know what to call it. We are -- both our clients and we are all Roman Catholics, and we observe a holiday. Yesterday it was Remembrance Day and today is All Saints Day, and we all participate in the prayers, and we usually go to the church to pray. Today we'd like to do it, because the service in the church will be at 3.00. So could we perhaps make a different kind of break, to stop at 2.00 -- or rather, to begin the afternoon session at 2.00 and then work until 3.00 so we could make it to the church, because the church closing at 4.00, or to try to make some other arrangement. I don't know. I do apologise. Perhaps you will think that it is out of place, but we would really like to get to the church for about half an hour for the prayer to remember our dead. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have no objection. Counsel consulted me this morning before you came in, and we have no objection to some reasonable accommodation to that. If we could perhaps start -- maybe lose a bit time at the end of day but also maybe pick up a bit of it by starting -- maybe taking a shorter lunch. But in any event, whatever the Judges -- Your Honours' wishes are, we do not object to some accommodation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And on the side of the Judges, we also have some problems. We have some other obligations during the lunch break, and we were told that it is impossible for us to hold afternoon session tomorrow afternoon because this courtroom is arranged for another case. So at this moment, we have a suggestion to make. We will have no sitting this afternoon, as well as tomorrow afternoon, but we will make it up next Friday afternoon, the Friday afternoon of next week. Is that acceptable to all parties? Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do you want me to tell you except to say thank you very much. Of course it is acceptable. Thank you. Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we would ask -- the only thing we could ask, please, is that -- we'd appreciate the accommodation of my learned friends on the other side in terms of at least finishing the witness that would probably start then today. We have a witness coming from Bosna. Well, who is here from Bosnia. My concern -- I expect to start him sometime this morning when the cross-examination is completed. My concern would be, of course, that without this afternoon whether we would finish him by 1.00 tomorrow, and again it would be an unfortunate situation where he would have to stay here over the weekend. So I just ask some accommodation from my learned friends about possibly assuring, if they can, that the cross-examination be concluded tomorrow morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik. We're all in your hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. I can promise that our cross-examination of this witness and the next witness will be finished in time. With the witness who is present here, you will see for yourselves. I will be exceptionally brief, and I will do my best to be brief with the next witness. I will respect all the wishes expressed. And I should also like to thank Their Honours for granting us this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. I am the counsel for the accused Naletilic, and I shall ask you some questions. I say this to every witness. I try to phrase them as short as possible so that your answers can be as short as possible. But because we both speak the same language, will you please make a pause after you hear my question to allow for the interpretation to avoid overlapping. Thank you very much for your understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask, please, the usher to put Prosecutor's Exhibit 20.2 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, my first question, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Will you now please take the pointer -- oh, you have it. Good. Now, if you can identify any of these buildings, or you work here, will you please point out to us where you were?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, I shall try to point at the building, but I cannot be certain that it is the building, because when we were brought there, we were not allowed to look around. We were taken straight up to the door, and we were not allowed to turn around or look around ourselves. So that with all the reservations, I think it is this building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I will tell you very openly why I am asking you that. You mentioned hangars or something, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hangars, yes. I'm sorry, I was too fast. The hangars that I mentioned yesterday is what I heard from those that we were together with for a meal in this chief building in which I was. They were brought there, 30, 50, 100 men at a time, together, their meal, and they were saying that they were in the hangar number 1, 2, 3, or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Where is that?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Sorry. Do you mean this former military secondary school at the Heliodrom or, broadly, the territory covered by Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't mean one building, I mean the whole compound, the whole area covered by Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, as you can see, there are no hangars here. It was the Soko factory.

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, I made no tours of the area. I didn't have the opportunity to see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So that is something that you were told by others; you do not have any knowledge of your own?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: People who were detained there and who were brought under escort to eat in the canteen in the cellar of this building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: All right. Will you tell us, please, a few words about this canteen. How many meals did you have a day, and what was the food like?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think -- no, I don't think -- I'm sure that a few days after the Red Cross visited us and brought parcels, that we began to have some meals in the canteen. I think there were three meals a day. However, the chief meal -- rather, the principal food was what we had been donated by the Red Cross representatives, and that was rather meager.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So we can say that insofar as food was concerned, it was quite all right?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after these first two or three days, under the circumstances, the food that we were getting was quite decent because we had no -- we really did not think much of the quality or anything else after that starvation that we went through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean during those first two days?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, during those first two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did anyone bring you food privately? I mean you personally. Did you get food from any other source?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when we were driven out, rounded up from our flats, and when we headed for the stadium, other people had some bags with clothes, but my -- because nobody knew what would happen to us. My mother had taken a few loaves of bread and some tinned sardines and taken that along. When we were arrive at the Heliodrom and when we were locked up in the cells, and then when we learned for certain after I had seen in the cellar many women and children downstairs in the cellars, and after I was told that my family was also there, then through some guards who used to be my neighbour, he did bring us some food from downstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean during those two days?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I have to tell you that, of course, I shared it with other people, because it is enough for a man to have one bite or two just to feel that they have taken in something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. I understand that. Tell me, you told the Honourable Court yesterday how some humanitarian organisations came, and the television recorded it all and that that was an opportunity to have the children out and to make them play and then this was all recorded, and that nearby there was a van or something with some oranges and biscuits and the like. So could you tell me which television ran this programme and when was it done? Because you told us that your sister had seen it.

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the HTV, and that is when they found out that we were at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So it was the HTV, and it was the 10th of May, the 10th until you left? You were there for about 20 days.

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: 9th -- 9th -- as of 9th of May. So it could have been four or five days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right. So we can look for this tape at the HTV?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But as I was saying, your wife and your mother left about ten days, just as all women and children did, if I understood you well.

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So it would have been eight to ten. Maybe seven or eight days, except for seven women who left at the same time we did. Those were women of some age and allegedly they were mothers of soldiers fighting on the other side, and they were released at the same time when -- with us, because they were on the same bus with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And after those seven and eight days, there were no more women and children at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And your mother and your wife were not harmed by anyone? They were treated decently?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you can call it that. They were detained and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, no, no. Of course. That is out of the question.

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no physical contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, you are an educated man, aren't you? I'm mindful of your identity, and the -- but you are an educated man, and I am -- I want you to explain to me -- as a mater of fact, I don't have too many questions, but the differences, the inconsistencies between your statements -- oh, no. Let me ask you this: Do you remember the statement that you gave to the AID on the 8th of August, 1996?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Then let me remind you. In that statement, you never once mentioned either Juka Prazina or Mr. Naletilic or Franjo Greguric or Minister Tadic, nor this thing with children. All the rest is, I must admit, is consistent with what you said today. Now, this first statement in 1996, I presume that your memory was fresher then than it is today. However, my question is: Did you tell all the truth in 1996, everything that you knew then?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know if they wrote it down, because of course my memory must have been fresher at that time and all these impressions were still much more vivid, and I believe that my more extensive -- that I even told more than I did to the Prosecutors of this Tribunal. Why they did not note it down, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But -- so you read it and signed it. You had no objections at the time when you signed it. You could have objected then, couldn't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, under the circumstances, few of us looked at what they were signing and what --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, but it was the 8th of August, 1996, and that was a statement to your people. It was not foreigners or strangers that you were making the statement to.

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regardless, what they wanted to get from me was, I guess, some facts. They did not want to note any details. And when this comes to my children, my neighbours, people who lived around me, I think these -- this is detail which I'm certain of and not forget. I may forget certain things, but what happened to me, what happened to my children, to my family, I'm quite positive they'll forget that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Sir, I deeply sympathise with you, but my question is: Why didn't you tell AID, and then the investigators come, and you tell them the events in a completely different -- no. I mean you mention the names that you never before mentioned, and then you repeat them before this Court. Now, my question is: Are you still claiming that Mr. Greguric, the Prime Minister of the Republic of Croatia, together with Mr. Rajic, the President of the HDZ, was in the camp and that you saw him there, did you?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And his explanation I remember well. An elderly man who was sitting on the floor next to the door, and when they entered the cell, he even smiled a little and said, "Don't tell me you're a conscript too." Because this man looked of quite an age. That man was of Serb origin, and he said that he wasn't 60 yet. That is why I remember this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let us repeat it for the record. Mr. Franjo Greguric, the Prime Minister of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And Mr. Rajic was with him?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: And he wasn't the only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right. But you mentioned the two of them. You didn't mention this in your first statement. That is what I'm trying to check now. You also said that you were visited by the minister of -- Minister Tadic who was the minister for refugees, that he came there with a group of Americans. Would you please tell us what group of Americans was it, and where could we perhaps find them?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain this. This group of Americans had all military office badges. That is, they were also in uniforms, and they introduced themselves as Americans. And even there was one in uniform, 50-ish, tall, fat, big, fair haired.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: He was an American?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were told that they were Americans.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, this incident that you told about to the investigators for the first time, that event that Tuta's soldiers were somewhere, that you heard some noise or something, you never saw Tuta, did you? How do you know that they were Tuta's soldiers? Because yesterday, if I understood you properly, you only heard that they were Tuta's soldiers, that you did not know it of your own knowledge.

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember well, I was very precise yesterday and said how I found that out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, but that's what I'm trying to establish. You found that out.

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found that out, but it was from the guards because we heard this noise. So I heard it from guards that they were Tuta's soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, that was the only thing that I wanted to clarify. Nothing else. Witness GG, I will ask you something very frankly, which may be perhaps a little unusual for this kind of cross-examination. You do not Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. like Mr. Misic particularly, do you?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean? I do not like him? Perhaps I feel sorry for him because of what he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm asking you that because you gave almost three different versions of his visit to the camp, and they show that, to put it very mildly, you do not think highly of that man, that you dislike him, that perhaps you hate him, or that you feel sorry for him. The first time you said that Mr. Misic had come, before you had come out, and said that the fate of Muslims and Croats was tied together, whatever you might think of it. That was in your first statement that you gave to the AID. In your second statement to the investigators, you described the identical event, that is, Misic comes, and now you are asked whether you will be released, as in the first statement. You say that he told you, Well, if everything is all right, then you will be released. But if not everything is all right, what he thought or what you thought, that he was a member of the BH army or something, that such would be sent either to Zenica or to their grave.

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain that. Misic must have known me from somewhere. And when he appeared in the passage, a group of his neighbours from Balinovac told him, Major, let us go. And he explained to them that they were being interrogated, all the rest. But when he saw me, he came up to me directly the day my wife and children and the rest of my family were released -- rather, were about to be released and were released. And I wanted to seize that opportunity. And since I saw that he knew me, since he had come up to me, then I said, Major, could I also go with my family? How can they go on their own? And he said, No, you won't be in any trouble if you were never in the army. We shall question you and there will be no problem. But whoever belonged to the army, it will be either Zenica or the grave. And then -- may I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, please, do go on.

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then he did a round of the cells and said we have to live together. We cannot live one without the other. And as far as I know, whether it was that day or perhaps the day before, there was a meeting at Medjurgorje where they were precisely discussing the cessation of hostilities or something or cease-fire or an end to this conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much for your answer, but I asked you something else. What you just explained -- this is the first time what you are telling us because in the first statement, there's only one sentence. In the second statement, there is a different statement. And yesterday, you did not mention it at all. But I do not want to insist on this, so I'm coming to my last question. You said that this release -- and we know that 80 percent of all the men who were not members of the BH army left the camp after 20 days; only the members of the BH army stayed on at the Heliodrom. So my question is, You say that an agreement had been reached between the lawful authorities of the HZ HB and the BH army, that is, representatives of the two armies, that is, representatives of the two authorities with the mediation of General Morillon. This is my last question. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is how -- what we were told down there. But let me just add, it wasn't the members of the BH army left at the Heliodrom. The majority were released. As soon as Morillon left, people, they were taken back to the cells. That is once General Morillon was there, even the majority of the army members were released. But a few days later, they were rounded up again and brought back to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That is what I was saying, because there was an understanding to disband the camp. And you started, well, with Medjurgorje. But then it was said that only members of the BH army after your release -- I mean, towards the end of May at the Heliodrom, there were only members of the BH army at long last. Perhaps, you didn't understand very well.

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for your answers. Your Honours, I do not have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examination, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness GG, let me take you back to the 9th of May when you had to leave your apartment. Did you see -- did you take a good look at the soldiers who had kicked you out of the apartment and then lined you up in front of the building?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that, in fact, I had known a number of these men by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you see the uniforms that they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were the HVO uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did they all wear the same uniforms? I mean the same camouflage or some combination with the drab olive uniforms?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is hard for me to answer that. I did not pay that much attention. And in fact, I did not dare look much. But I believe that they are all were wearing camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: When you said that you did not dare look much, how did you have to behave?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were kicked out of our apartments. Then this column was formed and we were told to march, and we were not allowed to look left or right. Those were the orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And where was the column formed?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right there in front of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know who formed it?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who had kicked us out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said that you did not have any detailed knowledge of the uniforms. Did they have any special insignia on their uniforms, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said that you saw Vinko Martinovic. Where was he standing?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we exited the building, it would have been to the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Was he alone?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Was he closer to the road or closer to the entrance of the building?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Closer to the entrance, maybe 1 or 2 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you notice what he was doing?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to me, he stood and controlled the unfolding of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said that he had ordered someone to leave the column. Was that before you left or what? Once you got going? Please tell us what happened.

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a journalist, and he called him by name to get out the column once the column got going. It was -- and then after that, he was sent back to the column and we continued marching.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. Can we go into the private session for just the next couple of questions, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did anyone else -- can anyone else in addition to you corroborate this story that you just told us, from people in the column?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody in the column saw this. All my neighbours did, saw this journalist.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned Ernest Takac. Did you know him before the war, that is, before the Bosniak and Croat conflict?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew him by sight because he frequently came to the neighbourhood. I had no contact with him, but I came to know him well, because both while he was a civilian and later on, he behaved in a very arrogant way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you see him since the war, in the years since? Can we agree that he was prone to violence, that he was out of control?

utterances.speaker: Witness GG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that his behaviour during any contact I had with him was not normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I don't have any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Witness, for giving the evidence. When the usher pulls down the blinds, he will take you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you to this Honourable Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, do you have any documents to tender at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour. I don't have any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And who will deal with the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: May it please, the Court. Mr. President, the next witness requests to testify with the protective measures of -- to have his facial image protected and testify using a pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I guess there is no objections from Defence counsels. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your request is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please brief us with the relevance in the indictment at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Your Honour, this witness will give testimony in evidence concerning the background parts of the indictment, paragraph 7, as well as paragraphs 10 to 11; superior authority, paragraphs 14 to 16; general allegations, paragraphs 18 to 20; count 1, paragraph 26 to 29, and 34(a) and 34(b); and counts 2 through 8, paragraphs 35 to 40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, good morning. The usher is going to show you now a piece of paper that has your name on it. I should advise you that the Chamber has granted your request for protective measures in this, that your correct name, your actual name, will not be used anywhere on the record so that your identity will be protected, and you will also have your facial image protected in terms of the broadcast or the video record. In order to do that or to confirm, nonetheless, your identity for the record, I'm going to ask you to look at this paper and simply answer yes or no, is that your name? Don't state your name, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, in that regard, in that same regard, Witness -- and you will be referred to, I believe, as -- I believe it will be HH. As I just explained to you, Witness, you will be referred to in these proceedings as HH, again to protect your identity. In that regard, let me advise you, please, to be mindful of using -- you might inadvertently use your name or the name of a close family member or something that might tend to identify you. So please be mindful of that, if you could, for your own protection. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness HH, is it correct that you are a person of Bosniak ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You were born in Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And where did you grow up, at least most of the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: In my hometown.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what is that or was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Bivolje Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell us, just very roughly speaking, because many of us may not familiar with that particular village or location, where is that in relation to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: That was in the municipality of Capljina, and the village borders on the Mostar municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: And it is 25 kilometres from the approaches to Mostar, from the municipal line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Witness HH, I'm not going to ask you anything further about your background or residence, again not to tend to identify you any further. Is it correct, sir, that immediately prior to the outbreak of the armed conflict in Mostar in early May of 1993, around that time you were living in a flat or apartment in East Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it also correct, sir, that you joined the territorial defence on the 19th of September, 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it also correct that you then joined the HVO for a short time in approximately August or September, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you briefly explain to the Chamber why you joined the HVO at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Because the units of the TO at that time had to be reconfigured as the HVO units.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Why do you say "they had to be"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: This happened exactly after the HOS General Blaz Kraljevic was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And how was it that, again, that the TO forces -- you felt that you were required at that point to join the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Well, we simply received a summons to all appear at the particular location where we used to come. And we were told very briefly and simply that from that day on, we were the first battalion of the Capljina Brigade, and that was it. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who told you this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: The commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Mirsad Zubovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Had he formally been a member of the territorial defence himself, or was he an HVO officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: At that time, he became overnight an HVO officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And I take it by your answer, then, correct me if I misunderstand, that prior to that time he was an officer in the territorial defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did he explain to you how it was, as you say, that overnight he became -- he went from being a territorial defence officer to being an HVO officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: He did not explain anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that you, in fact, resigned or left the HVO a short time -- a short time after this when the HVO attacked Prozor in approximately September 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I left the HVO in September 1992 approximately, on the 12th or on the 13th. I cannot remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, Witness HH, I'm going to jump forward for a moment just to give the Chamber a bit of the setting of your overall testimony. Is it correct, sir, that on the 10th of May, 1993, you were arrested in Mostar by the HVO and taken to the MUP station there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes, that is also correct, in the night of the 10th of May, 1993, around 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm going to come back to that in a moment in more detail. Is it also correct that on about the 14th of May, you were moved from Mostar, from the MUP station, to another detention facility at Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Approximately, the 13th or the 14th. It was in the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And further, is it correct that on about the 27th of May, about, you were then moved from Ljubuski to the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes. That was a group of about 110 men, for the most part from Sovici, and we were told that we were going to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Then did you then remain a prisoner at the Heliodrom for some time after the 27th of May, for some months after the 27th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, as I mentioned to you, Witness, just so you're not confused, I'll come back to those things in more detail in a few minutes. Is it correct, sir, that during the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina that as many as 40 members of your family or close friends were killed or tortured during that war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes, including my immediate family and my extended family and my friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, is it correct that from about the fall of 1992 until April 1993, you were aware that there were growing tensions through this time between the Croats and the Bosniaks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware. And this is the reason why I did not want to take part in that conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is it correct that at some points, at some points in time and at various locations, these tensions from time to time broke out into actual fighting, such as Gornji Vakuf in approximately January 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes. That was approximately in early January, even though it was -- from what we learned, even though it was difficult to have much information in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm going to direct your attention now, moving more to the core of your testimony, I'm going to direct your attention to April of 1993. About the middle of that month, did things take a substantial turn for the worse, if you will? Did the conflict between the Bosniaks and the Croats become more intense at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Approximately from what I recall, after all these years, that was 17 or 18 April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What happened, as you recall, on the 17th and 18th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: In that period, several people were arrested, actually, three of my friends during that period, between the 17th to 18th and the 23rd, by -- I don't know whether this was a civilian police or the HVO police. I really am not sure who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Without being able to be more specific about that, do you associate the people who arrested them with, we might say, the Bosnian/Croat side, whether they were civilian police or whether they were HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: According to their own words, they were military policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And with the HVO, then, is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Who is "they"?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you told us just a moment ago that three of your friends were arrested by somebody. Who arrested them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I believe that question has been asked and answered. He answered it was the military police. With that objection, I would just also like to point out I have been very patient with my learned colleague because it has been background information so far. However, Mr. Scott is beginning to get into testimony, and I will be objecting to leading questions in the future. But I think this question has been asked and answered. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott. Can you lead us directly to the 10th of May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We are getting there very quickly, Your Honour, but there are a couple of questions this witness can help us with a few days before the 10th of May. I agree that the question was answered, Mr. President, but then the witness hesitated, and there may have been some confusion about who these people arresting these parties were. So that's why I went back and asked him again to clarify. When he said his three friends were arrested, he said military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of what organisation, of what side or group, were these military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So you don't know whether they were Bosnian -- whether they were Bosniak police, or Croat police, or you have no idea?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, can you please tell us anything else that happened around the 17th of April, 1993? Were there attacks, and if so, can you tell us anything you know about those attacks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: At that time, I was not a member of any unit. There was some exchange of fire and there was -- some people were killed, but the only thing I know is that my friends were released on the 23rd.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall from your time -- during this time other attacks on Herzegovina occurring around the middle of April 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: As far as I recall, on the 17th or 18th of April, there was the incident at Sovici, in the Jablanica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you also tell us, around this time do you know -- was there any attacks or armed action concerning a building called the Vranica building in Mostar? Not on the 9th and 10th of May but some weeks before that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: It was at that time, roughly between the 17th or 18th until the 23rd, it happened. It was some kind of an introduction, an overture to the war. There were some skirmishes. People were arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Okay. As part of this you just said overture to the war, did it involve an attack on the Vranica building around the 18th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: I really have nothing to do with it. I have no idea whether the building was attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right and do you recall whether there was an HVO action at a place called Gubavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes. That happened in the early morning of the 19th of November -- sorry, 19th April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell us briefly what you know happened at Gubavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: At that time at Gubavica, detachments, that is units of the Capljina Brigade, the HVO attacked the command, and people from the Bregava Brigade manned the front lines opposing the Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you lose any member of your family in that action, when the HVO attacked Gubavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes, a rather close relative.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. I'm not going to ask you to mention the name or go further than that at this time. Now, you've mentioned these friends that were arrested were then released on about the 23rd of May, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Or excuse me. 23rd of April. My mistake. Around the 23rd of April.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber what you know of any negotiations occurring between the Bosniak side and the HVO side around that time which may have contributed to these persons being released?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: At that time, during those skirmishes and arrests, negotiations took place, and as far as I can remember, Mr. Ejup Ganic was in Mostar, and they managed to bring the tension down, and they agreed on the joint command of the HVO and the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell the Chamber, who may not be familiar with this particular name up to this point in the trial, who was Mr. Ganic, and what was his position at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: He was the vice-president of the Republic -- no. The vice-president of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Was he a Bosniak, a Serb, or a Croat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Why, he was a Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, directing your attention then some days forward, can you tell us where you were on the 8th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: On the 8th of May, 1993, I was in West Mostar, in the immediate vicinity of the students' hostel, visiting with relatives. It was natural to cross the river after the truce and after these negotiations and the joint command, because the tension had abated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct that during the evening of the 8th of May, that is, you would say between the 8th of May and the 9th of May, that you spent the night at the apartment of these friends?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened on the morning of the 9th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Early in the morning on the 9th of May, we were awakened by shots, by detonations. There was shooting all around, and I realised that something terrible had happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I may have -- sorry. You answered that. And what were you able to observe? I assume if you woke up and got out of bed, were you able to look outside? Were you able to look around? Can you tell the Chamber more of what you saw happening at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: What happened was that when I woke up after those detonations - because it was a ground-floor flat in that building, so that the glass panes broke - we had to lie down on the floor. We dared not move because there was gunfire from all around. One could hear detonations nearby. That is all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell us, again without giving us too much detail, was the flat where you were staying at this time and where you were and what you're telling us just now, was this flat close to a building called the Vranica building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: About 100, 150 metres east of Vranica building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And directing your attention to about 11.00 on the 9th of May, 1993, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: 9th of May?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: 1993? At what time?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Around 11.00, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I must have heard wrongly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I will repeat the question. You've told us, Witness, that you spent the night between the 8th and 9th of May at this apartment in West Mostar near the Vranica building, that there was fire that woke you up. I'm directing your attention later that morning at approximately 11.00. What happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Oh. The next day, they came, broke the door. I mean, three masked men. They were looking for weapons. We were lying on the floor and said we had no weapons, but they said that we had to stay on the floor and not leave the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me ask you a couple of clarifications, please. Let's do get the date correct. Perhaps I misspoke. You said -- just now you said "the next day." Are you telling us what -- when these people came into the apartment that that was on the 10th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: I said -- I said that on the 9th of May, in the morning, when the HVO attack started and the Croatian army and aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And that started on the 9th of May. But when you tell us now that some people came into -- some soldiers came into the apartment where you were staying, was that on the 9th of May or on the 10th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: That happened twice during the -- on the 9th of May sometime in daytime, and in the evening of the 10th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's talk about the first time. Tell us more what happened the first time that these soldiers came into your apartment, or the apartment where you were staying.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: They did not come. They broke into the flat looking for weapons. I said so a while ago. And they told us that we had to stay on the floor, that we were not to go out anywhere, and we went by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could you identify these soldiers by anything that they said or wore as to what military unit or army they were part of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Those men were in camouflage uniforms. I'm not sure but perhaps one of them had a black uniform. They had very clearly the HB badges, not the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did they have anything else about their persons as part of their uniform or about them that you believe also identified them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: They had small flags, tiny flags, on one of the shoulders, on the shoulders or on the upper arm somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of what country were these flags?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Of the Croatian State.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So they came into the apartment looking for weapons, told you to lay down on the floor. What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: What happened? Well, there was gunfire all day long. We could not really get any food or even have some water because that was the ground floor of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, take us, forward, please now -- you said this happened twice. Take us to the second time, please, that any soldiers entered this flat.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: The second time, they came, pulled my cousin and me out, and that was in the evening of the 10th, that is, the next day. Then they told us to put our hands at the back of our heads, put us against the wall. And at the -- in the -- as I was coming out of the flat, I saw a man lying on the ground. He had been wounded, and I recognised two persons who were also in that passage. And I recognised doctor/surgeon Martinovic who was trying to lend aid to the man lying on the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Before you go forward with your story, will you please assist us, if you can, the soldiers that came on the evening of the 10th of May, were you able to observe anything that led you to believe what army or unit they were from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: One of them had a markedly Dalmatian pronunciation. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you draw any particular conclusion from that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Why, of course I did. If that soldier speaks dalmatian dialect, then it means that the Croatian army is in the vicinity and that he, himself, is a member of the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, going forward then, you said you were taken out, put against the wall, and you said you saw some things. There was a man lying in the passage, I believe you said. So tell us more about what you saw at that time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: As I came out of the flat, to the left was the door into the other flat, and there was a soldier lying -- I don't know which one, I'm not sure. It was a soldier in a camouflage uniform. And in that small hallway in that area, there were two more persons. And there was Dr. Martinovic, a surgeon who was aiding the person lying on the floor. And other members were beating those other two in the immediate vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Let's, again, get a bit more clarification. You said that there was a soldier lying on the floor.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you know which -- again, which army or military force that soldier was from, the one that you say was lying on the floor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: He was a member of the BH army. His name was Avdo Cehic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Then you said you saw some people being beaten. Who were they? And I don't necessarily mean by name, but by description or who were these other persons who were being beaten at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: One was 55, close to 60, and another one was a boy of 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: At the time you saw these men either lying on the floor or being beaten, were any of them armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you hear the name or come to know the name of one of the -- I'll give you either option -- either HV or HVO soldiers you saw in the passage at that time? Did you come to know the name of one those persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: I'll never forget that. The person who beat the worst was short; he was small. He lacked his front teeth, fair haired. The one, I mean, who spoke the dalmatian dialect.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you recall, did you hear a name or a nickname for this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: People addressed him as "Splico".

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you ever see this Splico again? And later on, again, in other parts of your testimony that we'll get to. Later on after this event, did you see this Splico again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: I saw him at the Heliodrom. While I was detained at the Heliodrom in the central prison, I saw him there a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you recall in what capacity was this Splico when you saw him? Was he there as a guard or a prisoner or what, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: At the very beginning of my detention in the central prison at the Heliodrom, he came as a soldier. Wasn't ashamed of it. I think he was very proud to have only the HV on his sleeve. And then all of a sudden, he was locked up above us, whether he was a prisoner there, was he there to squeal on us, to inform on us. I have no idea what he was doing on the upper floor of the prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, what happened next, then, after you saw these men being beaten and this Splico? What happened to you after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Me and my relative, the one that I was in the flat with, took out, this elderly man and this boy of 17, with our hands at the back of our heads, and they took us to the police building which was in the immediate vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Was this a building of the Herceg-Bosna civilian police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And were you left there, you and this other man -- or, excuse me, these other men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: They took us into the yard, the yard in front of that building, and we had to stand there like this with our hands up, and that is where I experienced the first blow. I have no idea. I'm saying I'll never forget it, because I've never had any trouble with anyone before, but then I was kicked here on the left. And before I realised what was happening, everybody around was on me and beating me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately how many other prisoners or persons were being detained at the police station when you arrived there or shortly thereafter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: At the very beginning, that moment when we entered this yard, there was a small room which served as a depot or something, a storage place, a very narrow one, and there were a few civilians. I can't remember how many, but a few civilians were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what happened after that? Were any of you taken for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: They first took that elderly man for interrogation. Then they took my cousin, but he didn't stay there long. And then my turn came.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what happened to you when they came for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: As I entered first up the stairs, then I reached a passage, and in the doorway of the room, the first room or office - I don't know really what to call it properly - I heard a shot fired in that office.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: And a person came up to me and said, "You're the next one."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Continue on, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: I was taken over by persons. I don't know how many of them. It is difficult to say. There were some lamps inside. It was all arranged. This passage was full of policemen and camouflage uniforms. So it's difficult to say. I couldn't really. I had to keep my head down and my hands on my head all the time, but they took me into a room and said they'd show me a videotape and that I'd recognise myself on that videotape.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What was this a videotape of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: That videotape was about a troop review or some oath of allegiance of members of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if I understand you well, they showed you this videotape and they asked you what, to identify people if you could?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: They said that I'd find myself on the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Well, naturally I did not find myself on that tape. I did not recognise myself there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were you then beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: After that, as far as I can remember, they told me to take -- they gave me a piece of paper and a pencil and told me to write a CV of a kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Go on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: And as far as I can remember, I then wrote down, naturally, what I knew about myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And how long did you stay in this room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Well, it's hard to tell, but I remember well how that person who gave me that piece of paper and the pencil, as I was writing, was opposite the table and that person's name was Vinko Beno.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I want to move forward quickly, Witness HH, if we ask. Let me just ask you again: During the time that you were in that room, at any point in time were you then beaten by police officers or soldiers in the room?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours. I have two objections. One, that is a very leading question, and it's the second time he's asked the question. He got -- he didn't get an answer he wanted, now he's repeated the leading question two times, and I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is the second time you've asked the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It is, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness HH, did anything else happen to you before being taken out of that room when all this came to an end?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: After I'd written that statement, the gentleman I recognised in front of me, and I'm 100 per cent sure of that, Mr. Vinko Beno, a person showed me a badge, a badge which had an Islamic temple on it, and he asked me, "Do you know what this is?" And I paused a little and then I said, "Well, that is a house of prayer." And then he said, "Balija, isn't -- ain't it a mosque?" And I never received such a blow at the nape of my neck. That could be dealt only by a professional.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Where were you taken after this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: After that, after that, they took me -- the gentleman said that I could wash myself a little. I did. And then they took me back into that small room which they called Pascara.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Well, they called that area over there in that yard, that place, that small area which had no door to it even.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, they called it, you said, Pascara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And perhaps, Witness HH, either you or if the Translation Unit can please help us, can you give us a --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It is a kennel, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: A kennel.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes. That's it more or less. A doghouse, a kennel, a house for a dog.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And what happened to you after that, Witness HH? How long did you stay in this Pascara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: That same night when I was brought there, the night of the 10th to the 11th I returned, my relative and that elderly man had already been brought back to this room, and I also spotted a lady sitting on a chair outside, and she wasn't there when we had arrived there first.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I can just ask one or two more questions to finish on this item.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you came back to this room or area called the Pascara, were there any other prisoners that had been brought there, either during your absence or perhaps they arrived a short time after you returned. Perhaps you can explain.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: There was this lady sitting in that chair, and there was Mr. Rudolf Jozelic, who is a Catholic, and there were a few of -- a few more people, and the faces of some I knew and the faces of others I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can just ask you again. Is there any other -- can you name any of the others that were there that you saw at that time, apart from the one that you've mentioned so far by name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would suggest that that would be a good place to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will resume at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness HH, directing your attention to the 11th of May, did a truck arrive in the vicinity of where you were being held? And if so, can you just tell us what happened in that regard.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Approximately on the 11th, between 9.00 and 12.00 in the morning, a truck arrived with a lot of equipment, and an order was given that we unload this equipment into -- and place it in a garage or a storage room. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you participate, in fact, in doing that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes, I did. And while I worked -- actually, until the time, I only had my undershirt on and my trunks, and I was barefoot.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were you able, around this time, because of the things that you were unloading, were you able to find some clothing to put on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes, I found a pair of pants which were fairly short. I put them on, and some kind of a shirt. And I still had no footwear to put on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Was it stated to you or did you come to know around this time where this material that was being unloaded from the truck, where that had come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: The lady who was sitting -- that lady who was sitting there all the time while we were there in that kennel, as we called it, she was sitting outside. And she told us that this was from the 4th Corps headquarters that this material had come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you see any women prisoners around this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Well, that is the lady that I have been referring to all this time. She was sitting outside, outdoors, in a chair all that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I want to direct you forward on the 11th of May. Did you go back to a room -- again, a room that had some sort of videorecorder in it and, if so, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: The same night -- actually, no, the day when we unloaded that, this was the first time that we got something to eat, as far as I recall. And on the evening of the 11th, a soldier came, a person in a black uniform, and this person took me -- I cannot recall where. I know that it was dark. The person was wearing a black uniform, and I was again taken to be interrogated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Briefly, what happened during the interrogation? You don't have to tell us everything that happened in detail, but will you just tell us a bit about what happened to you then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes. In addition to the person who led me to the interrogation, there were an additional two persons, very strongly built, who were there. They told me -- the two persons that I could see, that is -- they said, Balija, you will now recognise yourself in this cassette as a member of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, around that time, or at any time during the course of events you're telling us about now, did you know or come to know the names or identities of any of these persons who were questioning you at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: At that moment, as this tape was played back to me, this was a videocassette from the outtaking of the 42nd Mountain Brigade in the village of Bujeca [phoen], I did recognise myself on that tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, and what happened next? Actually, my question to you -- listen to my question, please. Were you able to identify any of the people who were questioning you at that time, the people who were in the room with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: The person who had brought me there and the two persons who I saw there for the first time in that room, it was -- they said that I should be taken over by a person named Lovric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And did you identify any of the other persons that were in this room around this time or that did anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: The person who took me over with Mr. Lovric and Mr. Vinko Beno was mentioned previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who was Vinko Beno, and how was he involved in this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: He was a former policeman of the former state of Yugoslavia. And at that time, he was with the Herceg-Bosna police but was originally from the Capljina municipality. He was born in the village of Rovna or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What did he do or what role did he play during the events when you were being held -- being taken to this room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: When it was said that this Mr. Lovric should take me over and the gentleman in the black uniform and another two persons whom I was unable to -- whose faces I was unable to make out, but they were very powerfully built. It's hard for me to say this because this is -- I would not like anyone to experience this. I prefer not to talk about this. I rarely bring this up, and this is a very terrible thing that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, let me stop you there, because I'm not going to ask you to tell us in detail about what happened, and with the Chamber's indulgence. Were you treated very badly during this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Animals are not treated the way those gentlemen treated me on that occasion. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask you, and again I'm not asking you to describe what happened to you because I'm going to respect your wishes on that, and I will certainly be in the Chamber's hands whether they wish it to be further pursued or not, did you know or come to know the identities of the two men who did these things to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: In addition to the identity of a person of Niko Beno, of which I'm 100 per cent certain, I learned later that those two persons were Ernest Takac and Romeo Blazevic, who was born in Donja Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How did you come to know either then or later that that was the -- that these were the identities of these two men, that is, Blazevic and Takac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: When we were transferred to Ljubuski. It was shortly thereafter, a day or two later at Ljubuski. The person who knew both of them -- and we were all standing in a circle in that prison in Ljubuski, and these two persons came to drink "balija blood," as they said. And the person standing next to me who knew them well received blows by those two. And I told him -- I asked him whether he knew them, and he said their names. This is how I learned who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me ask you some clarifying questions on that. Do I understand you correctly, Witness HH, to be saying then that you saw these same two men in Ljubuski a few days later beating someone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: These were the same men who had done these things to you in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, going back to -- we still have you now at the moment at the MUP station or at this place in Mostar. Were you then moved to another location around this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: I was not moved from that small room, but others were moved from my room to other rooms. They were rearranging us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Witness, what I'd like to do, please, to move forward, you've told us earlier at the beginning of your testimony, so I'll come back to it now, was it around this time that you were then moved from the MUP station in Mostar to a detention facility at Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Can you please repeat that question again?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course. Sometime after being mistreated in the way that you've told us, was it around this time that you were then moved from the MUP station in Mostar and taken to another camp or prison at Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes. When I came to, I was handcuffed with my left hand to another person, and we were already on our way to Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately how many other -- well, were there other prisoners on this, however it was, however you were being transported -- were you on a bus or a truck, or how were you being transported to Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: It was a large-sized van seating about 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And were there other prisoners with you when you regained consciousness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: In addition to my cousin and these two men who were together in the building where I was arrested and the lady who was sitting up front, there was a group of journalists of Radio Mostar there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you know why the journalists from Radio Mostar were in this van?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: I really don't know why they were there, but there were both men and women among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And perhaps I should make it clear. Were they there -- did you understand them to be there as journalists? I mean, were they there to report what was happening or were they on the van -- or in the van - excuse me - as prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: They were prisoners, just as I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you know if these persons were Bosniak or Croat or other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Among them -- it is hard to distinguish by the name and ethnic background. They had names like Dragan, Zoran, but I remember Alija Lizde was among them, Dzemo Hamzic, a lady called Bojana, a lady called Selma, and some other lady. There was another lady, Spomenka Drljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you arrive at the Ljubuski camp sometime in the evening between the 13th and the 14th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes, during that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And as you were being brought into the facility around that time, did you come to know or identify someone who was one of the -- either the head or one of the senior officials at that facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: When we arrived in this camp at that building, my handcuffs were taken off. I could barely stand on my feet, and we were asked to spread our legs and stand against a wall. At that point, I wasn't able to do so, and I received a blow -- a kick in the leg. And I turned around and said that this hurt. And as I turned around, I recognised Mr. Zdenko Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How is it that you recognised him? Did you know him from before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: I knew him from before because he worked at a gas station in Tasocici.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you come to know any of the other guards at the Ljubuski facility while you were being held there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: While I was there, on one -- there was one who was nicknamed Struja. And the other one had no qualms about identifying himself by the last name of Petrovic, and he was one of the policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The women that were in the van with you, were they kept with you in the same cells, or do you know if they were taken to another part of the facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: From what I remember, they were in the same building but at the top floor, same entrance, but at the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, around the 22nd of May, 1993, if I can direct your attention to that, were you taken to perform forced labour at a place called Hrasno?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And briefly tell the Chamber, please, what happened to you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: When we arrived in the village of Hrasno, there was -- at the line of separation between the HVO and -- how shall I call them -- Chetniks ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Go ahead. What did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: We were making bunkers. We were carrying rock, filling sandbags. And at one point, a very strongly built man appeared. We were hungry and thirsty, and I asked whether we could have something to drink. And he said, Balija -- some called us balijas, others called us Turks. He said, Now I'll give you something to drink. And then I was forcibly fed -- I think it was at least half a litre of a spirit of -- some kind of brandy which they poured down my throat.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you become drunk?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: I almost lost consciousness because I rarely ever touched alcohol.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what happened to you after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: After that, in that condition, I was - I don't know - inebriated or something. They brought me in front of a bunker facing the Chetnik line, and they tied me to a tree. And I spent all day tied to that tree, and they played with me. There was shooting coming from both sides, and I spent all day there tied to a tree in a temperature close to 30 degrees Celsius.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The tree that you were tied to, was this between the HVO line and the Serb line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS HH
utterances.text: Yes, it was, but it was closer to the HVO bunkers, that is, the positions of the Grude battalion.
